sections.title: Never ship a hook-only command
sections.content: PreRun/PersistentPreRun only execute when Run/RunE is declared. A command intended to do work must declare Run — otherwise the hooks silently never fire.

sections.title: Prefer stdlib + pflag; dependencies need justification

sections.title: Hook order is PersistentPreRun, PreRun, Run, PostRun, PersistentPostRun
sections.content: command.go execute() runs them in that order. Persistent*Run hooks inherit down the tree — a child without its own PersistentPreRun gets the parent's. All hooks only fire if the command declares Run/RunE. Note the asymmetry: parent PersistentPreRun fires for children, but PersistentPostRun runs only if the *executed* command's chain reaches it.

sections.title: Regenerate doc/ output when commands change
sections.content: Man/markdown/yaml docs are generated from the live command tree — stale generated docs are a defect. Re-run the generator after command/flag changes.

sections.title: PersistentFlags inherit to children; local Flags do not
sections.content: cmd.PersistentFlags() propagate down the whole subtree — the idiomatic place for --verbose/--config style globals. Local flags on Flags() apply only to that command. InheritedFlags()/LocalFlags() split them for introspection and help output.

sections.title: Commands form a tree resolved by ExecuteC and find()
sections.content: Command is a node: root.Execute() -> ExecuteC walks args via find() to resolve the target subcommand, then calls execute(). TraverseChildren controls whether args are parsed as flags during descent or treated strictly as command names until the target is found.

sections.title: SetContext flows ctx through ExecuteC to every hook
sections.content: root.SetContext(ctx) before Execute; every Command.Context() returns it inside Run/hooks. ExecuteContext is the all-in-one entry. Cancellation propagates to command execution — the right way to wire signal handling into a cobra app.

func genFishComp(buf io.StringWriter, name string, includeDesc bool) {
	// Variables should not contain a '-' or ':' character
	nameForVar := name
	nameForVar = strings.ReplaceAll(nameForVar, "-", "_")
	nameForVar = strings.ReplaceAll(nameForVar, ":", "_")

	compCmd := ShellCompRequestCmd
	if !includeDesc {
		compCmd = ShellCompNoDescRequestCmd
	}
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf("# fish completion for %-36s -*- shell-script -*-\n", name))
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf(`
function __%[1]s_debug
    set -l file "$BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE"
    if test -n "$file"
        echo "$argv" >> $file
    end
end

function __%[1]s_perform_completion
    __%[1]s_debug "Starting __%[1]s_perform_completion"

    # Extract all args except the last one
    set -l args (commandline -opc)
    # Extract the last arg and escape it in case it is a space or wildcard
    set -l lastArg (string escape -- (commandline -ct))

    __%[1]s_debug "args: $args"
    __%[1]s_debug "last arg: $lastArg"

    # Disable ActiveHelp which is not supported for fish shell
    set -l requestComp "%[10]s=0 $args[1] %[3]s $(string join ' ' -- (string escape -- $args[2..-1])) $lastArg"

    __%[1]s_debug "Calling $requestComp"
    set -l results (eval $requestComp 2> /dev/null)

    # Some programs may output extra empty lines after the directive.
    # Let's ignore them or else it will break completion.
    # Ref: https://github.com/spf13/cobra/issues/1279
    for line in $results[-1..1]

func genFishComp(buf io.StringWriter, name string, includeDesc bool) {
	// Variables should not contain a '-' or ':' character
	nameForVar := name
	nameForVar = strings.ReplaceAll(nameForVar, "-", "_")
	nameForVar = strings.ReplaceAll(nameForVar, ":", "_")

	compCmd := ShellCompRequestCmd
	if !includeDesc {
		compCmd = ShellCompNoDescRequestCmd
	}
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf("# fish completion for %-36s -*- shell-script -*-\n", name))
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf(`
function __%[1]s_debug
    set -l file "$BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE"
    if test -n "$file"
        echo "$argv" >> $file
    end
end

function __%[1]s_perform_completion
    __%[1]s_debug "Starting __%[1]s_perform_completion"

    # Extract all args except the last one
    set -l args (commandline -opc)
    # Extract the last arg and escape it in case it is a space or wildcard
    set -l lastArg (string escape -- (commandline -ct))

    __%[1]s_debug "args: $args"
    __%[1]s_debug "last arg: $lastArg"

    # Disable ActiveHelp which is not supported for fish shell

	c.iflags = nil
	c.parentsPflags = nil
}

Active help must degrade cleanly without env support
sections.content: Active help emits via completion machinery; it must no-op when COBRA_ACTIVE_HELP=0 or the shell lacks support — never break completion to deliver hints.

sections.title: Do not put cleanup in root PersistentPostRun expecting it to run for children
sections.content: Cleanup shared across subcommands belongs in each command's own PostRun or a wrapper around Execute — PersistentPostRun on root does not reliably cover children.

sections.title: Commands form a tree resolved by ExecuteC and find()
sections.content: Command is a node: root.Execute() -> ExecuteC walks args via find() to resolve the target subcommand, then calls execute(). TraverseChildren controls whether args are parsed as flags during descent or treated strictly as command names until the target is found.

sections.title: SetContext flows ctx through ExecuteC to every hook
sections.content: root.SetContext(ctx) before Execute; every Command.Context() returns it inside Run/hooks. ExecuteContext is the all-in-one entry. Cancellation propagates to command execution — the right way to wire signal handling into a cobra app.

sections.title: Only persistent flags propagate to subcommands
sections.content: Local flags declared via Flags() stay on their command; PersistentFlags() are visible to the whole subtree.

sections.title: E-suffixed hooks return errors; plain variants do not
sections.content: RunE/PreRunE/PostRunE/PersistentPreRunE/PersistentPostRunE return error, propagated to ExecuteC's return. Plain Run/PreRun/etc return nothing. If both are set the E variant wins. Non-E hooks are for commands that handle errors internally.

sections.title: Cobra runs hooks around Run in a fixed order
sections.content: PersistentPreRun, PreRun, Run, PostRun, PersistentPostRun — persistent variants inherit to children that don't declare their own.

sections.title: Active help streams hints into shell completion
sections.content: active_help.go: programs set messages via GetActiveHelpConfig/ActiveHelp; the __complete machinery emits them as completion descriptions. Controlled by the COBRA_ACTIVE_HELP env var (0 disables, 'local' limits to local commands).

    __%[1]s_debug "Starting __%[1]s_perform_completion"

sections.title: CLI-visible changes are breaking for downstream CLIs

sections.title: SilenceUsage and SilenceErrors control post-error output
sections.content: Command.SilenceUsage suppresses usage printing on error; SilenceErrors suppresses the error echo. Common pattern: SilenceUsage=true once execution has started (usage spam only makes sense for parse errors). Root-level silence gives the app full control of error formatting.

sections.title: Only persistent flags propagate to subcommands
sections.content: Local flags declared via Flags() stay on their command; PersistentFlags() are visible to the whole subtree.

sections.title: Hooks never fire on commands without Run
sections.content: A Command with only PersistentPreRun and no Run/RunE is a no-op — the whole hook chain is gated on Run being declared. Adding a stub Run is required for hook-only commands.

func Gt(a interface{}, b interface{}) bool {
	var left, right int64
	av := reflect.ValueOf(a)

	switch av.Kind() {
	case reflect.Array, reflect.Chan, reflect.Map, reflect.Slice:
		left = int64(av.Len())
	case reflect.Int, reflect.Int8, reflect.Int16, reflect.Int32, reflect.Int64:
		left = av.Int()
	case reflect.String:
		left, _ = strconv.ParseInt(av.String(), 10, 64)
	}

	bv := reflect.ValueOf(b)

	switch bv.Kind() {
	case reflect.Array, reflect.Chan, reflect.Map, reflect.Slice:
		right = int64(bv.Len())
	case reflect.Int, reflect.Int8, reflect.Int16, reflect.Int32, reflect.Int64:
		right = bv.Int()
	case reflect.String:
		right, _ = strconv.ParseInt(bv.String(), 10, 64)
	}

	return left > right
}

func genFishComp(buf io.StringWriter, name string, includeDesc bool) {
	// Variables should not contain a '-' or ':' character
	nameForVar := name
	nameForVar = strings.ReplaceAll(nameForVar, "-", "_")
	nameForVar = strings.ReplaceAll(nameForVar, ":", "_")

	compCmd := ShellCompRequestCmd
	if !includeDesc {
		compCmd = ShellCompNoDescRequestCmd
	}
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf("# fish completion for %-36s -*- shell-script -*-\n", name))
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf(`
function __%[1]s_debug
    set -l file "$BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE"
    if test -n "$file"
        echo "$argv" >> $file
    end
end

function __%[1]s_perform_completion
    __%[1]s_debug "Starting __%[1]s_perform_completion"

    # Extract all args except the last one
    set -l args (commandline -opc)
    # Extract the last arg and escape it in case it is a space or wildcard
    set -l lastArg (string escape -- (commandline -ct))

    __%[1]s_debug "args: $args"
    __%[1]s_debug "last arg: $lastArg"

    # Disable ActiveHelp which is not supported for fish shell
    set -l requestComp "%[10]s=0 $args[1] %[3]s $(string join ' ' -- (string escape -- $args[2..-1])) $lastArg"

    __%[1]s_debug "Calling $requestComp"
    set -l results (eval $requestComp 2> /dev/null)

    # Some programs may output extra empty lines after the directive.
    # Let's ignore them or else it will break completion.

    for line in $results[-1..1]

func genFishComp(buf io.StringWriter, name string, includeDesc bool) {
	// Variables should not contain a '-' or ':' character
	nameForVar := name
	nameForVar = strings.ReplaceAll(nameForVar, "-", "_")
	nameForVar = strings.ReplaceAll(nameForVar, ":", "_")

	compCmd := ShellCompRequestCmd
	if !includeDesc {
		compCmd = ShellCompNoDescRequestCmd
	}
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf("# fish completion for %-36s -*- shell-script -*-\n", name))
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf(`
function __%[1]s_debug
    set -l file "$BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE"
    if test -n "$file"
        echo "$argv" >> $file
    end
end

function __%[1]s_perform_completion
    __%[1]s_debug "Starting __%[1]s_perform_completion"

    # Extract all args except the last one
    set -l args (commandline -opc)
    # Extract the last arg and escape it in case it is a space or wildcard
    set -l lastArg (string escape -- (commandline -ct))

    __%[1]s_debug "args: $args"

sections.title: Global flags belong on PersistentFlags, not local Flags
sections.content: Flags that must be usable from any subcommand (verbose, config, output format) go on root's PersistentFlags — local Flags() do not inherit.

sections.title: Test commands with SetArgs + buffers, never subprocess
sections.content: cmd.SetArgs, cmd.SetOut/SetErr(bytes.Buffer), then Execute(). Fresh Command instance per test — flag state persists across Execute calls on the same instance.

sections.title: Shared flags must be PersistentFlags on the root command
sections.content: If a flag should work on every subcommand, declare it via root.PersistentFlags() — local Flags() never inherit.

sections.title: PersistentFlags vs Flags: inheritance boundary
sections.content: Anything meant for the whole CLI goes on PersistentFlags — Flags() definitions are per-command only.

sections.title: Only persistent flags propagate to subcommands
sections.content: Local flags declared via Flags() stay on their command; PersistentFlags() are visible to the whole subtree.

sections.title: Hooks never fire on commands without Run
sections.content: A Command with only PersistentPreRun and no Run/RunE is a no-op — the whole hook chain is gated on Run being declared. Adding a stub Run is required for hook-only commands.

func genFishComp(buf io.StringWriter, name string, includeDesc bool) {
	// Variables should not contain a '-' or ':' character
	nameForVar := name
	nameForVar = strings.ReplaceAll(nameForVar, "-", "_")
	nameForVar = strings.ReplaceAll(nameForVar, ":", "_")

	compCmd := ShellCompRequestCmd
	if !includeDesc {
		compCmd = ShellCompNoDescRequestCmd
	}
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf("# fish completion for %-36s -*- shell-script -*-\n", name))
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf(`
function __%[1]s_debug
    set -l file "$BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE"
    if test -n "$file"
        echo "$argv" >> $file
    end
end

function __%[1]s_perform_completion
    __%[1]s_debug "Starting __%[1]s_perform_completion"

    # Extract all args except the last one
    set -l args (commandline -opc)
    # Extract the last arg and escape it in case it is a space or wildcard
    set -l lastArg (string escape -- (commandline -ct))

    __%[1]s_debug "args: $args"
    __%[1]s_debug "last arg: $lastArg"

    # Disable ActiveHelp which is not supported for fish shell
    set -l requestComp "%[10]s=0 $args[1] %[3]s $(string join ' ' -- (string escape -- $args[2..-1])) $lastArg"

    __%[1]s_debug "Calling $requestComp"
    set -l results (eval $requestComp 2> /dev/null)

    # Some programs may output extra empty lines after the directive.
    # Let's ignore them or else it will break completion.
    # Ref: https://github.com/spf13/cobra/issues/1279
    for line in $results[-1..1]

func Gt(a interface{}, b interface{}) bool {
	var left, right int64
	av := reflect.ValueOf(a)

	switch av.Kind() {
	case reflect.Array, reflect.Chan, reflect.Map, reflect.Slice:
		left = int64(av.Len())
	case reflect.Int, reflect.Int8, reflect.Int16, reflect.Int32, reflect.Int64:
		left = av.Int()
	case reflect.String:
		left, _ = strconv.ParseInt(av.String(), 10, 64)
	}

	bv := reflect.ValueOf(b)

	switch bv.Kind() {
	case reflect.Array, reflect.Chan, reflect.Map, reflect.Slice:
		right = int64(bv.Len())
	case reflect.Int, reflect.Int8, reflect.Int16, reflect.Int32, reflect.Int64:
		right = bv.Int()
	case reflect.String:
		right, _ = strconv.ParseInt(bv.String(), 10, 64)
	}

	return left > right
}

func manPreamble(buf io.StringWriter, header *GenManHeader, cmd *cobra.Command, dashedName string) {
	description := cmd.Long
	if len(description) == 0 {
		description = cmd.Short
	}

	cobra.WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf(`%% "%s" "%s" "%s" "%s" "%s"
# NAME
`, header.Title, header.Section, header.date, header.Source, header.Manual))
	cobra.WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf("%s \\- %s\n\n", dashedName, cmd.Short))
	cobra.WriteStringAndCheck(buf, "# SYNOPSIS\n")
	cobra.WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf("**%s**\n\n", cmd.UseLine()))
	cobra.WriteStringAndCheck(buf, "# DESCRIPTION\n")
	cobra.WriteStringAndCheck(buf, description+"\n\n")
}

sections.title: Active help must degrade cleanly without env support
sections.content: Active help emits via completion machinery; it must no-op when COBRA_ACTIVE_HELP=0 or the shell lacks support — never break completion to deliver hints.

sections.title: Commands form a tree resolved by ExecuteC and find()
sections.content: Command is a node: root.Execute() -> ExecuteC walks args via find() to resolve the target subcommand, then calls execute(). TraverseChildren controls whether args are parsed as flags during descent or treated strictly as command names until the target is found.

sections.title: E-suffixed hooks return errors; plain variants do not
sections.content: RunE/PreRunE/PostRunE/PersistentPreRunE/PersistentPostRunE return error, propagated to ExecuteC's return. Plain Run/PreRun/etc return nothing. If both are set the E variant wins. Non-E hooks are for commands that handle errors internally.

sections.title: Hook order is PersistentPreRun, PreRun, Run, PostRun, PersistentPostRun
sections.content: command.go execute() runs them in that order. Persistent*Run hooks inherit down the tree — a child without its own PersistentPreRun gets the parent's. All hooks only fire if the command declares Run/RunE. Note the asymmetry: parent PersistentPreRun fires for children, but PersistentPostRun runs only if the *executed* command's chain reaches it.

func genZshComp(buf io.StringWriter, name string, includeDesc bool) {
	compCmd := ShellCompRequestCmd
	if !includeDesc {
		compCmd = ShellCompNoDescRequestCmd
	}
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf(`#compdef %[1]s
compdef _%[1]s %[1]s

# zsh completion for %-36[1]s -*- shell-script -*-

__%[1]s_debug()
{
    local file="$BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE"
    if [[ -n ${file} ]]; then
        echo "$*" >> "${file}"
    fi
}

_%[1]s()
{
    local shellCompDirectiveError=%[3]d
    local shellCompDirectiveNoSpace=%[4]d
    local shellCompDirectiveNoFileComp=%[5]d
    local shellCompDirectiveFilterFileExt=%[6]d
    local shellCompDirectiveFilterDirs=%[7]d
    local shellCompDirectiveKeepOrder=%[8]d

    local lastParam lastChar flagPrefix requestComp out directive comp lastComp noSpace keepOrder
    local -a completions

    __%[1]s_debug "\n========= starting completion logic =========="
    __%[1]s_debug "CURRENT: ${CURRENT}, words[*]: ${words[*]}"

    # The user could have moved the cursor backwards on the command-line.
    # We need to trigger completion from the $CURRENT location, so we need
    # to truncate the command-line ($words) up to the $CURRENT location.
    # (We cannot use $CURSOR as its value does not work when a command is an alias.)
    words=("${=words[1,CURRENT]}")
    __%[1]s_debug "Truncated words[*]: ${words[*]},"

sections.title: Test commands via SetArgs + SetOut/SetErr buffers
sections.content: The idiom: cmd.SetArgs([]string{...}), cmd.SetOut(buf), cmd.SetErr(buf), then Execute(). Works without subprocess; assert on buf contents and the returned error. Remember a fresh command instance per test — flag state persists across Execute calls.

sections.title: SilenceUsage and SilenceErrors control post-error output
sections.content: Command.SilenceUsage suppresses usage printing on error; SilenceErrors suppresses the error echo. Common pattern: SilenceUsage=true once execution has started (usage spam only makes sense for parse errors). Root-level silence gives the app full control of error formatting.

func writePreamble(buf io.StringWriter, name string) {
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf("# bash completion for %-36s -*- shell-script -*-\n", name))
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf(`
__%[1]s_debug()
{
    if [[ -n ${BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE:-} ]]; then
        echo "$*" >> "${BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE}"
    fi
}

# Homebrew on Macs have version 1.3 of bash-completion which doesn't include
# _init_completion. This is a very minimal version of that function.
__%[1]s_init_completion()
{
    COMPREPLY=()
    _get_comp_words_by_ref "$@" cur prev words cword
}

__%[1]s_index_of_word()
{
    local w word=$1
    shift
    index=0
    for w in "$@"; do
        [[ $w = "$word" ]] && return
        index=$((index+1))
    done
    index=-1
}

__%[1]s_contains_word()
{
    local w word=$1; shift
    for w in "$@"; do
        [[ $w = "$word" ]] && return
    done
    return 1
}

sections.title: Hook order is PersistentPreRun, PreRun, Run, PostRun, PersistentPostRun
sections.content: command.go execute() runs them in that order. Persistent*Run hooks inherit down the tree — a child without its own PersistentPreRun gets the parent's. All hooks only fire if the command declares Run/RunE. Note the asymmetry: parent PersistentPreRun fires for children, but PersistentPostRun runs only if the *executed* command's chain reaches it.

func TestBashCompletions(t *testing.T) {
	rootCmd := &Command{
		Use:                    "root",
		ArgAliases:             []string{"pods", "nodes", "services", "replicationcontrollers", "po", "no", "svc", "rc"},
		ValidArgs:              []string{"pod", "node", "service", "replicationcontroller"},
		BashCompletionFunction: bashCompletionFunc,
		Run:                    emptyRun,
	}
	rootCmd.Flags().IntP("introot", "i", -1, "help message for flag introot")
	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.MarkFlagRequired("introot"))

	// Filename.
	rootCmd.Flags().String("filename", "", "Enter a filename")
	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.MarkFlagFilename("filename", "json", "yaml", "yml"))

	// Persistent filename.
	rootCmd.PersistentFlags().String("persistent-filename", "", "Enter a filename")
	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.MarkPersistentFlagFilename("persistent-filename"))
	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.MarkPersistentFlagRequired("persistent-filename"))

	// Filename extensions.
	rootCmd.Flags().String("filename-ext", "", "Enter a filename (extension limited)")
	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.MarkFlagFilename("filename-ext"))
	rootCmd.Flags().String("custom", "", "Enter a filename (extension limited)")
	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.MarkFlagCustom("custom", "__complete_custom"))

	// Subdirectories in a given directory.
	rootCmd.Flags().String("theme", "", "theme to use (located in /themes/THEMENAME/)")

func Gt(a interface{}, b interface{}) bool {
	var left, right int64
	av := reflect.ValueOf(a)

	switch av.Kind() {
	case reflect.Array, reflect.Chan, reflect.Map, reflect.Slice:
		left = int64(av.Len())
	case reflect.Int, reflect.Int8, reflect.Int16, reflect.Int32, reflect.Int64:
		left = av.Int()
	case reflect.String:
		left, _ = strconv.ParseInt(av.String(), 10, 64)
	}

	bv := reflect.ValueOf(b)

	switch bv.Kind() {
	case reflect.Array, reflect.Chan, reflect.Map, reflect.Slice:
		right = int64(bv.Len())
	case reflect.Int, reflect.Int8, reflect.Int16, reflect.Int32, reflect.Int64:
		right = bv.Int()
	case reflect.String:
		right, _ = strconv.ParseInt(bv.String(), 10, 64)
	}

	return left > right
}

    fi

    COMPREPLY=()
    _get_comp_words_by_ref "$@" cur prev words cword

    local requestComp lastParam lastChar args

func TestBashCompletions(t *testing.T) {
	rootCmd := &Command{
		Use:                    "root",
		ArgAliases:             []string{"pods", "nodes", "services", "replicationcontrollers", "po", "no", "svc", "rc"},
		ValidArgs:              []string{"pod", "node", "service", "replicationcontroller"},
		BashCompletionFunction: bashCompletionFunc,
		Run:                    emptyRun,
	}
	rootCmd.Flags().IntP("introot", "i", -1, "help message for flag introot")
	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.MarkFlagRequired("introot"))

	// Filename.
	rootCmd.Flags().String("filename", "", "Enter a filename")
	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.MarkFlagFilename("filename", "json", "yaml", "yml"))

	// Persistent filename.
	rootCmd.PersistentFlags().String("persistent-filename", "", "Enter a filename")
	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.MarkPersistentFlagFilename("persistent-filename"))
	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.MarkPersistentFlagRequired("persistent-filename"))

	// Filename extensions.
	rootCmd.Flags().String("filename-ext", "", "Enter a filename (extension limited)")
	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.MarkFlagFilename("filename-ext"))
	rootCmd.Flags().String("custom", "", "Enter a filename (extension limited)")
	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.MarkFlagCustom("custom", "__complete_custom"))

	// Subdirectories in a given directory.
	rootCmd.Flags().String("theme", "", "theme to use (located in /themes/THEMENAME/)")
	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.Flags().SetAnnotation("theme", BashCompSubdirsInDir, []string{"themes"}))

	// For two word flags check

	rootCmd.Flags().BoolP("two-w-default", "T", false, "this is not two word flags")

sections.title: Hook order is PersistentPreRun, PreRun, Run, PostRun, PersistentPostRun

func writePreamble(buf io.StringWriter, name string) {
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf("# bash completion for %-36s -*- shell-script -*-\n", name))
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf(`
__%[1]s_debug()
{
    if [[ -n ${BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE:-} ]]; then
        echo "$*" >> "${BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE}"
    fi
}

# Homebrew on Macs have version 1.3 of bash-completion which doesn't include
# _init_completion. This is a very minimal version of that function.
__%[1]s_init_completion()
{
    COMPREPLY=()
    _get_comp_words_by_ref "$@" cur prev words cword
}

__%[1]s_index_of_word()
{
    local w word=$1
    shift
    index=0
    for w in "$@"; do
        [[ $w = "$word" ]] && return
        index=$((index+1))
    done
    index=-1
}

__%[1]s_contains_word()
{
    local w word=$1; shift
    for w in "$@"; do
        [[ $w = "$word" ]] && return
    done
    return 1
}

__%[1]s_handle_go_custom_completion()
{
    __%[1]s_debug "${FUNCNAME[0]}: cur is ${cur}, words[*] is ${words[*]}, #words[@] is ${#words[@]}"

    local shellCompDirectiveError=%[3]d
    local shellCompDirectiveNoSpace=%[4]d
    local shellCompDirectiveNoFileComp=%[5]d
    local shellCompDirectiveFilterFileExt=%[6]d
    local shellCompDirectiveFilterDirs=%[7]d

    local out requestComp lastParam lastChar comp directive args

    # Prepare the command to request completions for the program.
    # Calling ${words[0]} instead of directly %[1]s allows handling aliases
    args=("${words[@]:1}")
    # Disable ActiveHelp which is not supported for bash completion v1
    requestComp="%[8]s=0 ${words[0]} %[2]s ${args[*]}"

    lastParam=${words[$((${#words[@]}-1))]}
    lastChar=${lastParam:$((${#lastParam}-1)):1}
    __%[1]s_debug "${FUNCNAME[0]}: lastParam ${lastParam}, lastChar ${lastChar}"

    if [ -z "${cur}" ] && [ "${lastChar}" != "=" ]; then
        # If the last parameter is complete (there is a space following it)
        # We add an extra empty parameter so we can indicate this to the go method.
        __%[1]s_debug "${FUNCNAME[0]}: Adding extra empty parameter"
        requestComp="${requestComp} \"\""
    fi

    __%[1]s_debug "${FUNCNAME[0]}: calling ${requestComp}"
    # Use eval to handle any environment variables and such
    out=$(eval "${requestComp}" 2>/dev/null)

    # Extract the directive integer at the very end of the output following a colon (:)
    directive=${out##*:}
    # Remove the directive
    out=${out%%:*}
    if [ "${directive}" = "${out}" ]; then
        # There is not directive specified
        directive=0
    fi
    __%[1]s_debug "${FUNCNAME[0]}: the completion directive is: ${directive}"
    __%[1]s_debug "${FUNCNAME[0]}: the completions are: ${out}"

    if [ $((directive & shellCompDirectiveError)) -ne 0 ]; then
        # Error code.  No completion.
        __%[1]s_debug "${FUNCNAME[0]}: received error from custom completion go code"
        return
    else
        if [ $((directive & shellCompDirectiveNoSpace)) -ne 0 ]; then
            if [[ $(type -t compopt) = "builtin" ]]; then
                __%[1]s_debug "${FUNCNAME[0]}: activating no space"
                compopt -o nospace
            fi
        fi
        if [ $((directive & shellCompDirectiveNoFileComp)) -ne 0 ]; then
            if [[ $(type -t compopt) = "builtin" ]]; then
                __%[1]s_debug "${FUNCNAME[0]}: activating no file completion"
                compopt +o default
            fi
        fi
    fi

    if [ $((directive & shellCompDirectiveFilterFileExt)) -ne 0 ]; then
        # File extension filtering
        local fullFilter filter filteringCmd
        # Do not use quotes around the $out variable or else newline
        # characters will be kept.
        for filter in ${out}; do
            fullFilter+="$filter|"
        done

        filteringCmd="_filedir $fullFilter"
        __%[1]s_debug "File filtering command: $filteringCmd"
        $filteringCmd
    elif [ $((directive & shellCompDirectiveFilterDirs)) -ne 0 ]; then
        # File completion for directories only
        local subdir
        # Use printf to strip any trailing newline
        subdir=$(printf "%%s" "${out}")
        if [ -n "$subdir" ]; then
            __%[1]s_debug "Listing directories in $subdir"
            __%[1]s_handle_subdirs_in_dir_flag "$subdir"
        else
            __%[1]s_debug "Listing directories in ."
            _filedir -d
        fi
    else
        while IFS='' read -r comp; do
            COMPREPLY+=("$comp")
        done < <(compgen -W "${out}" -- "$cur")
    fi
}

__%[1]s_handle_reply()
{
    __%[1]s_debug "${FUNCNAME[0]}"
    local comp
    case $cur in
        -*)
            if [[ $(type -t compopt) = "builtin" ]]; then
                compopt -o nospace
            fi
            local allflags
            if [ ${#must_have_one_flag[@]} -ne 0 ]; then
                allflags=("${must_have_one_flag[@]}")
            else
                allflags=("${flags[*]} ${two_word_flags[*]}")
            fi
            while IFS='' read -r comp; do
                COMPREPLY+=("$comp")
            done < <(compgen -W "${allflags[*]}" -- "$cur")
            if [[ $(type -t compopt) = "builtin" ]]; then
                [[ "${COMPREPLY[0]}" == *= ]] || compopt +o nospace
            fi

            # complete after --flag=abc
            if [[ $cur == *=* ]]; then
                if [[ $(type -t compopt) = "builtin" ]]; then
                    compopt +o nospace
                fi

                local index flag
                flag="${cur%%=*}"
                __%[1]s_index_of_word "${flag}" "${flags_with_completion[@]}"
                COMPREPLY=()
                if [[ ${index} -ge 0 ]]; then
                    PREFIX=""
                    cur="${cur#*=}"
                    ${flags_completion[${index}]}
                    if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
                        # zsh completion needs --flag= prefix
                        eval "COMPREPLY=( \"\${COMPREPLY[@]/#/${flag}=}\" )"

                fi
            fi

            if [[ -z "${flag_parsing_disabled}" ]]; then
                # If flag parsing is enabled, we have completed the flags and can return.

func TestBashCompletions(t *testing.T) {
	rootCmd := &Command{
		Use:                    "root",
		ArgAliases:             []string{"pods", "nodes", "services", "replicationcontrollers", "po", "no", "svc", "rc"},
		ValidArgs:              []string{"pod", "node", "service", "replicationcontroller"},
		BashCompletionFunction: bashCompletionFunc,
		Run:                    emptyRun,
	}
	rootCmd.Flags().IntP("introot", "i", -1, "help message for flag introot")
	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.MarkFlagRequired("introot"))

	// Filename.
	rootCmd.Flags().String("filename", "", "Enter a filename")
	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.MarkFlagFilename("filename", "json", "yaml", "yml"))

	// Persistent filename.
	rootCmd.PersistentFlags().String("persistent-filename", "", "Enter a filename")
	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.MarkPersistentFlagFilename("persistent-filename"))
	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.MarkPersistentFlagRequired("persistent-filename"))

	// Filename extensions.
	rootCmd.Flags().String("filename-ext", "", "Enter a filename (extension limited)")
	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.MarkFlagFilename("filename-ext"))
	rootCmd.Flags().String("custom", "", "Enter a filename (extension limited)")
	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.MarkFlagCustom("custom", "__complete_custom"))

	// Subdirectories in a given directory.
	rootCmd.Flags().String("theme", "", "theme to use (located in /themes/THEMENAME/)")
	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.Flags().SetAnnotation("theme", BashCompSubdirsInDir, []string{"themes"}))

sections.title: Hook order is PersistentPreRun, PreRun, Run, PostRun, PersistentPostRun
sections.content: command.go execute() runs them in that order. Persistent*Run hooks inherit down the tree — a child without its own PersistentPreRun gets the parent's. All hooks only fire if the command declares Run/RunE. Note the asymmetry: parent PersistentPreRun fires for children, but PersistentPostRun runs only if the *executed* command's chain reaches it.

func genFishComp(buf io.StringWriter, name string, includeDesc bool) {
	// Variables should not contain a '-' or ':' character
	nameForVar := name
	nameForVar = strings.ReplaceAll(nameForVar, "-", "_")
	nameForVar = strings.ReplaceAll(nameForVar, ":", "_")

	compCmd := ShellCompRequestCmd
	if !includeDesc {
		compCmd = ShellCompNoDescRequestCmd
	}
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf("# fish completion for %-36s -*- shell-script -*-\n", name))
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf(`
function __%[1]s_debug
    set -l file "$BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE"
    if test -n "$file"
        echo "$argv" >> $file
    end
end

function __%[1]s_perform_completion
    __%[1]s_debug "Starting __%[1]s_perform_completion"

    # Extract all args except the last one
    set -l args (commandline -opc)
    # Extract the last arg and escape it in case it is a space or wildcard
    set -l lastArg (string escape -- (commandline -ct))

    __%[1]s_debug "args: $args"
    __%[1]s_debug "last arg: $lastArg"

    # Disable ActiveHelp which is not supported for fish shell
    set -l requestComp "%[10]s=0 $args[1] %[3]s $(string join ' ' -- (string escape -- $args[2..-1])) $lastArg"

    __%[1]s_debug "Calling $requestComp"
    set -l results (eval $requestComp 2> /dev/null)

    # Some programs may output extra empty lines after the directive.
    # Let's ignore them or else it will break completion.

func TestBashCompletions(t *testing.T) {
	rootCmd := &Command{
		Use:                    "root",
		ArgAliases:             []string{"pods", "nodes", "services", "replicationcontrollers", "po", "no", "svc", "rc"},
		ValidArgs:              []string{"pod", "node", "service", "replicationcontroller"},
		BashCompletionFunction: bashCompletionFunc,
		Run:                    emptyRun,
	}
	rootCmd.Flags().IntP("introot", "i", -1, "help message for flag introot")
	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.MarkFlagRequired("introot"))

	// Filename.
	rootCmd.Flags().String("filename", "", "Enter a filename")
	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.MarkFlagFilename("filename", "json", "yaml", "yml"))

	// Persistent filename.

sections.title: Hook order is PersistentPreRun, PreRun, Run, PostRun, PersistentPostRun
sections.content: command.go execute() runs them in that order. Persistent*Run hooks inherit down the tree — a child without its own PersistentPreRun gets the parent's. func Gt(a interface{}, b interface{}) bool {
	var left, right int64
	av := reflect.ValueOf(a)

	switch av.Kind() {
	case reflect.Array, reflect.Chan, reflect.Map, reflect.Slice:
		left = int64(av.Len())
	case reflect.Int, reflect.Int8, reflect.Int16, reflect.Int32, reflect.Int64:
		left = av.Int()
	case reflect.String:
		left, _ = strconv.ParseInt(av.String(), 10, 64)
	}

	bv := reflect.ValueOf(b)

	switch bv.Kind() {
	case reflect.Array, reflect.Chan, reflect.Map, reflect.Slice:
		right = int64(bv.Len())
	case reflect.Int, reflect.Int8, reflect.Int16, reflect.Int32, reflect.Int64:
		right = bv.Int()
	case reflect.String:
		right, _ = strconv.ParseInt(bv.String(), 10, 64)
	}

	return left > right
}

func genFishComp(buf io.StringWriter, name string, includeDesc bool) {
	// Variables should not contain a '-' or ':' character
	nameForVar := name
	nameForVar = strings.ReplaceAll(nameForVar, "-", "_")
	nameForVar = strings.ReplaceAll(nameForVar, ":", "_")

	compCmd := ShellCompRequestCmd
	if !includeDesc {
		compCmd = ShellCompNoDescRequestCmd
	}
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf("# fish completion for %-36s -*- shell-script -*-\n", name))
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf(`
function __%[1]s_debug
    set -l file "$BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE"
    if test -n "$file"
        echo "$argv" >> $file
    end
end

function __%[1]s_perform_completion
    __%[1]s_debug "Starting __%[1]s_perform_completion"

    # Extract all args except the last one
    set -l args (commandline -opc)
    # Extract the last arg and escape it in case it is a space or wildcard
    set -l lastArg (string escape -- (commandline -ct))

    __%[1]s_debug "args: $args"
    __%[1]s_debug "last arg: $lastArg"

    # Disable ActiveHelp which is not supported for fish shell
    set -l requestComp "%[10]s=0 $args[1] %[3]s $(string join ' ' -- (string escape -- $args[2..-1])) $lastArg"

    __%[1]s_debug "Calling $requestComp"
    set -l results (eval $requestComp 2> /dev/null)

    # Some programs may output extra empty lines after the directive.
    # Let's ignore them or else it will break completion.
    # Ref: https://github.com/spf13/cobra/issues/1279
    for line in $results[-1..1]

sections.title: Hook order is PersistentPreRun, PreRun, Run, PostRun, PersistentPostRun
sections.content: command.go execute() runs them in that order. Persistent*Run hooks inherit down the tree — a child without its own PersistentPreRun gets the parent's. All hooks only fire if the command declares Run/RunE. Note the asymmetry: parent PersistentPreRun fires for children, but PersistentPostRun runs only if the *executed* command's chain reaches it.

sections.content: Currently, only one of the persistent pre-runs and post-runs is executed. (from commit 4cafa37bc4; touches cobra.go, command.go)

sections.title: Hook order is PersistentPreRun, PreRun, Run, PostRun, PersistentPostRun
sections.content: command.go execute() runs them in that order. Persistent*Run hooks inherit down the tree — a child without its own PersistentPreRun gets the parent's. All hooks only fire if the command declares Run/RunE. Note the asymmetry: parent PersistentPreRun fires for children, but PersistentPostRun runs only if the *executed* command's chain reaches it.

sections.title: Cobra runs hooks around Run in a fixed order
sections.content: PersistentPreRun, PreRun, Run, PostRun, PersistentPostRun — persistent variants inherit to children that don't declare their own.

sections.title: Hook lifecycle: persistent-pre, pre, run, post, persistent-post
sections.content: execute() in command.go fires PersistentPreRun then PreRun before Run, then PostRun and PersistentPostRun. Hooks are gated on Run being declared.

sections.title: Hooks never fire on commands without Run
sections.content: A Command with only PersistentPreRun and no Run/RunE is a no-op — the whole hook chain is gated on Run being declared. Adding a stub Run is required for hook-only commands.

sections.title: E-suffixed hooks return errors; plain variants do not
sections.content: RunE/PreRunE/PostRunE/PersistentPreRunE/PersistentPostRunE return error, propagated to ExecuteC's return. Plain Run/PreRun/etc return nothing. If both are set the E variant wins. Non-E hooks are for commands that handle errors internally.

sections.title: Only persistent flags propagate to subcommands
sections.content: Local flags declared via Flags() stay on their command; PersistentFlags() are visible to the whole subtree.

sections.title: SetContext flows ctx through ExecuteC to every hook
sections.content: root.SetContext(ctx) before Execute; every Command.Context() returns it inside Run/hooks. ExecuteContext is the all-in-one entry. Cancellation propagates to command execution — the right way to wire signal handling into a cobra app.

func TestBashCompletionTraverseChildren(t *testing.T) {
	c := &Command{Use: "c", Run: emptyRun, TraverseChildren: true}

	c.Flags().StringP("string-flag", "s", "", "string flag")
	c.Flags().BoolP("bool-flag", "b", false, "bool flag")

	buf := new(bytes.Buffer)
	assertNoErr(t, c.GenBashCompletion(buf))
	output := buf.String()

	// check that local nonpersistent flag are not set since we have TraverseChildren set to true
	checkOmit(t, output, `local_nonpersistent_flags+=("--string-flag")`)
	checkOmit(t, output, `local_nonpersistent_flags+=("--string-flag=")`)
	checkOmit(t, output, `local_nonpersistent_flags+=("-s")`)
	checkOmit(t, output, `local_nonpersistent_flags+=("--bool-flag")`)
	checkOmit(t, output, `local_nonpersistent_flags+=("-b")`)
}

func writePostscript(buf io.StringWriter, name string) {
	name = strings.ReplaceAll(name, ":", "__")
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf("__start_%s()\n", name))
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf(`{
    local cur prev words cword split
    declare -A flaghash 2>/dev/null || :
    declare -A aliashash 2>/dev/null || :
    if declare -F _init_completion >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        _init_completion -s || return
    else
        __%[1]s_init_completion -n "=" || return
    fi

    local c=0
    local flag_parsing_disabled=
    local flags=()
    local two_word_flags=()
    local local_nonpersistent_flags=()
    local flags_with_completion=()
    local flags_completion=()
    local commands=("%[1]s")
    local command_aliases=()
    local must_have_one_flag=()
    local must_have_one_noun=()
    local has_completion_function=""
    local last_command=""
    local nouns=()
    local noun_aliases=()

    __%[1]s_handle_word
}

`, name))
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf(`if [[ $(type -t compopt) = "builtin" ]]; then
    complete -o default -F __start_%s %s
else
    complete -o default -o nospace -F __start_%s %s
fi

`, name, name, name, name))

func TestBashCompletions(t *testing.T) {
	rootCmd := &Command{
		Use:                    "root",
		ArgAliases:             []string{"pods", "nodes", "services", "replicationcontrollers", "po", "no", "svc", "rc"},
		ValidArgs:              []string{"pod", "node", "service", "replicationcontroller"},
		BashCompletionFunction: bashCompletionFunc,
		Run:                    emptyRun,
	}

	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.MarkFlagRequired("introot"))

	// Filename.
	rootCmd.Flags().String("filename", "", "Enter a filename")
	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.MarkFlagFilename("filename", "json", "yaml", "yml"))

func genFishComp(buf io.StringWriter, name string, includeDesc bool) {
	// Variables should not contain a '-' or ':' character
	nameForVar := name
	nameForVar = strings.ReplaceAll(nameForVar, "-", "_")
	nameForVar = strings.ReplaceAll(nameForVar, ":", "_")

	compCmd := ShellCompRequestCmd
	if !includeDesc {
		compCmd = ShellCompNoDescRequestCmd
	}
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf("# fish completion for %-36s -*- shell-script -*-\n", name))
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf(`
function __%[1]s_debug
    set -l file "$BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE"
    if test -n "$file"
        echo "$argv" >> $file
    end
end

function __%[1]s_perform_completion
    __%[1]s_debug "Starting __%[1]s_perform_completion"

    # Extract all args except the last one
    set -l args (commandline -opc)
    # Extract the last arg and escape it in case it is a space or wildcard
    set -l lastArg (string escape -- (commandline -ct))

    __%[1]s_debug "args: $args"
    __%[1]s_debug "last arg: $lastArg"

    # Disable ActiveHelp which is not supported for fish shell
    set -l requestComp "%[10]s=0 $args[1] %[3]s $(string join ' ' -- (string escape -- $args[2..-1])) $lastArg"

    __%[1]s_debug "Calling $requestComp"
    set -l results (eval $requestComp 2> /dev/null)

    # Some programs may output extra empty lines after the directive.
    # Let's ignore them or else it will break completion.
    # Ref: https://github.com/spf13/cobra/issues/1279
    for line in $results[-1..1]

sections.title: PersistentFlags inherit to children; local Flags do not
sections.content: cmd.PersistentFlags() propagate down the whole subtree — the idiomatic place for --verbose/--config style globals. Local flags on Flags() apply only to that command. InheritedFlags()/LocalFlags() split them for introspection and help output.

sections.title: Commands form a tree resolved by ExecuteC and find()
sections.content: Command is a node: root.Execute() -> ExecuteC walks args via find() to resolve the target subcommand, then calls execute(). TraverseChildren controls whether args are parsed as flags during descent or treated strictly as command names until the target is found.

sections.title: E-suffixed hooks return errors; plain variants do not
sections.content: RunE/PreRunE/PostRunE/PersistentPreRunE/PersistentPostRunE return error, propagated to ExecuteC's return. Plain Run/PreRun/etc return nothing. If both are set the E variant wins. Non-E hooks are for commands that handle errors internally.

func manPreamble(buf io.StringWriter, header *GenManHeader, cmd *cobra.Command, dashedName string) {
	description := cmd.Long
	if len(description) == 0 {
		description = cmd.Short
	}

	cobra.WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf(`%% "%s" "%s" "%s" "%s" "%s"
# NAME
`, header.Title, header.Section, header.date, header.Source, header.Manual))
	cobra.WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf("%s \\- %s\n\n", dashedName, cmd.Short))
	cobra.WriteStringAndCheck(buf, "# SYNOPSIS\n")
	cobra.WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf("**%s**\n\n", cmd.UseLine()))
	cobra.WriteStringAndCheck(buf, "# DESCRIPTION\n")
	cobra.WriteStringAndCheck(buf, description+"\n\n")
}

func Gt(a interface{}, b interface{}) bool {
	var left, right int64
	av := reflect.ValueOf(a)

	switch av.Kind() {
	case reflect.Array, reflect.Chan, reflect.Map, reflect.Slice:
		left = int64(av.Len())
	case reflect.Int, reflect.Int8, reflect.Int16, reflect.Int32, reflect.Int64:
		left = av.Int()
	case reflect.String:
		left, _ = strconv.ParseInt(av.String(), 10, 64)
	}

	bv := reflect.ValueOf(b)

	switch bv.Kind() {
	case reflect.Array, reflect.Chan, reflect.Map, reflect.Slice:
		right = int64(bv.Len())
	case reflect.Int, reflect.Int8, reflect.Int16, reflect.Int32, reflect.Int64:
		right = bv.Int()
	case reflect.String:
		right, _ = strconv.ParseInt(bv.String(), 10, 64)
	}

	return left > right
}

sections.content: Command is a node: root.Execute() -> ExecuteC walks args via find() to resolve the target subcommand, then calls execute(). TraverseChildren controls whether args are parsed as flags during descent or treated strictly as command names until the target is found.

sections.title: SetContext flows ctx through ExecuteC to every hook
sections.content: root.SetContext(ctx) before Execute; every Command.Context() returns it inside Run/hooks. ExecuteContext is the all-in-one entry. Cancellation propagates to command execution — the right way to wire signal handling into a cobra app.

sections.title: E-suffixed hooks return errors; plain variants do not
sections.content: RunE/PreRunE/PostRunE/PersistentPreRunE/PersistentPostRunE return error, propagated to ExecuteC's return. Plain Run/PreRun/etc return nothing. If both are set the E variant wins. Non-E hooks are for commands that handle errors internally.

sections.title: Active help streams hints into shell completion
sections.content: active_help.go: programs set messages via GetActiveHelpConfig/ActiveHelp; the __complete machinery emits them as completion descriptions. Controlled by the COBRA_ACTIVE_HELP env var (0 disables, 'local' limits to local commands).

func Gt(a interface{}, b interface{}) bool {
	var left, right int64
	av := reflect.ValueOf(a)

	switch av.Kind() {
	case reflect.Array, reflect.Chan, reflect.Map, reflect.Slice:
		left = int64(av.Len())
	case reflect.Int, reflect.Int8, reflect.Int16, reflect.Int32, reflect.Int64:
		left = av.Int()
	case reflect.String:
		left, _ = strconv.ParseInt(av.String(), 10, 64)
	}

	bv := reflect.ValueOf(b)

	switch bv.Kind() {
	case reflect.Array, reflect.Chan, reflect.Map, reflect.Slice:
		right = int64(bv.Len())
	case reflect.Int, reflect.Int8, reflect.Int16, reflect.Int32, reflect.Int64:
		right = bv.Int()
	case reflect.String:
		right, _ = strconv.ParseInt(bv.String(), 10, 64)
	}

	return left > right
}

sections.content: Cleanup shared across subcommands belongs in each command's own PostRun or a wrapper around Execute — PersistentPostRun on root does not reliably cover children.

sections.title: PersistentFlags inherit to children; local Flags do not
sections.content: cmd.PersistentFlags() propagate down the whole subtree — the idiomatic place for --verbose/--config style globals. Local flags on Flags() apply only to that command. InheritedFlags()/LocalFlags() split them for introspection and help output.

sections.title: PersistentFlags vs Flags: inheritance boundary
sections.content: Anything meant for the whole CLI goes on PersistentFlags — Flags() definitions are per-command only.

    set -l file "$BASH_COMP_DEBUG_FILE"
    if test -n "$file"
        echo "$argv" >> $file
    end
end

function __%[1]s_perform_completion
    __%[1]s_debug "Starting __%[1]s_perform_completion"

    # Extract all args except the last one
    set -l args (commandline -opc)
    # Extract the last arg and escape it in case it is a space or wildcard
    set -l lastArg (string escape -- (commandline -ct))

func writePostscript(buf io.StringWriter, name string) {
	name = strings.ReplaceAll(name, ":", "__")
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf("__start_%s()\n", name))
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf(`{
    local cur prev words cword split
    declare -A flaghash 2>/dev/null || :
    declare -A aliashash 2>/dev/null || :
    if declare -F _init_completion >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        _init_completion -s || return
    else
        __%[1]s_init_completion -n "=" || return
    fi

    local c=0
    local flag_parsing_disabled=
    local flags=()
    local two_word_flags=()
    local local_nonpersistent_flags=()
    local flags_with_completion=()
    local flags_completion=()
    local commands=("%[1]s")
    local command_aliases=()
    local must_have_one_flag=()
    local must_have_one_noun=()
    local has_completion_function=""
    local last_command=""
    local nouns=()
    local noun_aliases=()

    __%[1]s_handle_word
}

`, name))
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, fmt.Sprintf(`if [[ $(type -t compopt) = "builtin" ]]; then
    complete -o default -F __start_%s %s
else
    complete -o default -o nospace -F __start_%s %s
fi

`, name, name, name, name))
	WriteStringAndCheck(buf, "# ex: ts=4 sw=4 et filetype=sh\n")
}

func TestBashCompletions(t *testing.T) {
	rootCmd := &Command{
		Use:                    "root",
		ArgAliases:             []string{"pods", "nodes", "services", "replicationcontrollers", "po", "no", "svc", "rc"},
		ValidArgs:              []string{"pod", "node", "service", "replicationcontroller"},
		BashCompletionFunction: bashCompletionFunc,
		Run:                    emptyRun,
	}
	rootCmd.Flags().IntP("introot", "i", -1, "help message for flag introot")
	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.MarkFlagRequired("introot"))

	// Filename.
	rootCmd.Flags().String("filename", "", "Enter a filename")
	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.MarkFlagFilename("filename", "json", "yaml", "yml"))

	// Persistent filename.
	rootCmd.PersistentFlags().String("persistent-filename", "", "Enter a filename")
	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.MarkPersistentFlagFilename("persistent-filename"))
	assertNoErr(t, rootCmd.MarkPersistentFlagRequired("persistent-filename"))

	// Filename extensions.
	rootCmd.Flags().String("filename-ext", "", "Enter a filename (extension limited)")

    __%[1]s_debug "Starting __%[1]s_perform_completion"

sections.content: root.SetContext(ctx) before Execute; every Command.Context() returns it inside Run/hooks. ExecuteContext is the all-in-one entry. Cancellation propagates to command execution — the right way to wire signal handling into a cobra app.
